claims.lede: <readme>evo-agents</readme> is open-source tooling for teams that work with Claude Code, Codex CLI or opencode. A <workers>worker</workers> on your own laptop or desktop takes plan steps from your team's hub, runs them with one of those agents and sends the log and the evidence back.
claims.planRuns: A <planRuns>plan run</planRuns> hands a whole plan to one worker, and the agent does its steps in the order the plan allows. As the agent reports a step, <verify>the worker runs the step's verify commands again</verify>, then commits and pushes. <timeout>The run's timeout</timeout> of 2, 4, 8 or 24 hours counts only the time the agent works.
claims.sleep: On macOS the worker <sleep>keeps the machine awake</sleep> while it holds a run. A laptop on battery with its lid closed sleeps anyway: its runs stop, and <retry>the hub tries them again</retry> once their leases run out.
claims.decisions: A plan run's agent stops for you only at <decisions>decisions of a few kinds</decisions>, such as deleting data, a migration on real data, sending to an outside service, spending money, or a choice of architecture or scope the plan leaves open. It makes every other choice itself and <why>writes down why</why> in the step's evidence.
claims.waiting: While you decide, the run <waits>waits, and the wait does not count toward its timeout</waits>. You answer in the <inbox>Inbox</inbox> on the web, or with <telegram>a button on Telegram</telegram> when the hub has a bot. After 24 hours without an answer the run <parks>parks and frees its slot on the worker</parks>, and a later answer resumes it in the same session.
claims.spool: With the <spool>evo-hub plugin</spool> in Claude Code, a successful Bash, Grep, WebFetch or MCP result longer than 10,000 characters is written whole to a file on your machine. The model gets <head>its first and last 1,500 characters</head> and a line that names the file.
claims.sessionPerStep: A plan run can also give <sessionPerStep>each step a session of its own</sessionPerStep>, which holds that step and the plan's handoff instead of everything the run read before it.
claims.graph: <harnessInit>evo-agents harness init</harnessInit> gives each repo of a project a source, and the harness one of its own, for one knowledge graph of the project. Agents query it over MCP: <kgSearch>kg_search</kgSearch> finds ids by name, code, path or words, and <kgImpact>kg_impact</kgImpact> lists what depends on a file or a diff before you change it.
claims.worktrees: In a <planRuns>plan run</planRuns> the agent works in a worktree of each repo the plan names, on the branch the plan gives that repo, so one plan can change several repos.
claims.install: <graphify>The graphify extra</graphify> gives the knowledge graph code symbols in about 40 languages, and <worker>the worker extra</worker> adds the worker's daemon.
claims.login: You <hubLogin>sign in once per machine</hubLogin>, and the token stays in ~/.evo/hub.
claims.plugins: <hubPlugin>evo-hub</hubPlugin> connects the agent to the hub's plans, and <kgPlugin>evo-kg</kgPlugin> to the project's knowledge graph. Codex takes the evo-hub plugin with <codex>two commands of its own</codex>.
claims.next: Then <quickStart>make a harness</quickStart> for your repos and <workers>pair a worker</workers>.
claims.roadmap: <roadmap>The roadmap</roadmap> says what works today and what is still being built, without dates.
claims.loop: <loop>The Loop</loop> turns changes in a project, such as a revised goal or a plan an agent wrote, into work for the kinds of run the hub already has, and asks people at three gates. It is in the code, off by default, and <roadmap>still changing</roadmap>.
claims.canvas: <canvas>Canvas</canvas> keeps a Lean Canvas for each product of a project, and a claim on it reaches validated only with real evidence. It is in the code, does nothing until an admin of the project enables it, and is <roadmap>still changing</roadmap>.
claims.growth: <growth>Growth plugins</growth> are not built yet: one would follow the people who come to a project on their own, and the other would post the project's news through its own accounts, with a check before each post and a cap on spending.
claims.status: evo-agents is early and before 1.0: <pypi>releases go to PyPI as evo-ak</pypi>, and commands, routes and file formats still change between them. The <license>code is Apache-2.0</license>, and you get access to a hub <invites>from an invite link or a hub admin</invites>.

unattended.title: Long work without anyone at the keyboard
unattended.need: People want agent work to keep going while they are away. Claude Code users asked for a session to go on once its session limit resets, and Claude Code now does that. A Show HN tool keeps a lid-closed Mac awake while agents work.

away.title: Questions that wait for an answer
away.need: Claude Code users reported a question that gave up after 60 seconds and went on without an answer. Others asked for a push to their phone when a permission approval waits.

context.title: Context that fills up
context.need: People ask for compaction they can steer, and for a way back to what it dropped. An article by Anthropic says that “getting agents to make consistent progress across multiple context windows remains an open problem.”
